land.purpose: Regional geographic base and decorative coastal coverage for the Rainforest to Rockies vector map.
land.processingCRS: EPSG:3005; NAD83 / BC Albers, always_xy true

features.land: GSHHG L1 marine footprint minus the final inland-water union. Major BC lakes and manmade waterbodies use official Freshwater Atlas polygons with island holes; overlapping older GSHHG lake bodies are replaced within BC. The identical compound geometry MUST own land fill and hatch clipping.
features.water: Official BC Freshwater Atlas lakes and manmade waterbodies selected at >=1 km², plus unmatched GSHHG lakes and GSHHG continuations outside BC. Island holes are retained. Intersected with GSHHG L1; no marine shoreline is taken from FWA.
features.bc: Statistics Canada digital administrative polygon, including marine jurisdiction; intersect with land for styling.
features.alberta: Statistics Canada digital administrative polygon; intersect with land for styling.
features.us: Complement of BC, Alberta and Saskatchewan digital regions inside this regional padded extent; includes any US context at frame corners. Intersect with land.
features.coastal-style: Broad decorative coverage from CWH/MH/CDF context plus marine area buffered 3 km; intersect with BC and land. Not a forest inventory.
features.saskatchewan: Statistics Canada digital administrative context for the small possible eastern frame fringe; rendering may use neutral land without this category.
features.data-coverage: Exact padded acquisition domain, including legitimate ocean. Use this footprint to verify coverage of the complete drawing canvas, including margins. The water feature remains inland water only; land union water is not acquisition coverage.

selection.areaInterpretation: AREA_HA is per source waterbody polygon, including any watershed partition; the threshold is not a merge by lake name.
selection.selectionSemantics: ArcGIS envelope queries return a conservative projected-envelope candidate set. Source ID/count completeness is exact for that service query; exact WGS84 geometry intersection and downstream clipping are separate operations.

sources.sourceGeometry: Full unsimplified service polygons; all original ring topology retained before processing.

selection.areaInterpretation: AREA_HA is per source waterbody polygon, including any watershed partition; the threshold is not a merge by lake name.
selection.selectionSemantics: ArcGIS envelope queries return a conservative projected-envelope candidate set. Source ID/count completeness is exact for that service query; exact WGS84 geometry intersection and downstream clipping are separate operations.

exactLocalSelection.explanation: The ArcGIS envelope query supplies a conservative candidate set. Exact local geometric clipping removes wholly outside candidates. The independent projected polygon query was checked by the acquisition agent against the same exact set.

preparation.landWater: Repair and clip source area geometry; densify long geographic segments at 0.1° before EPSG:3005 projection; snap overlays at 0.01 m. Use GSHHG L1 as sole marine footprint. Replace overlapping GSHHG lake bodies inside BC with official FWA lakes/manmade bodies selected at >=1 km²; preserve outside-BC continuations and unmatched GSHHG lakes. Subtract final water from L1, retaining island holes. Every connected source land/water piece enters one shared topology layer.
preparation.simplification: Mapshaper 0.8.10, Douglas-Peucker interval 125 m, keep-shapes and clean gap-fill-area=0. Final cleanup merged 75 narrow-channel islands into nearby land; exact source land and water topology was restored within 250 m of those components. No coast inset or blanket shoreline buffer is used.
preparation.admin: BC, Alberta and Saskatchewan digital regions simplified together at125m; derive the regional US complement. Digital marine-reaching provinces supply styling jurisdiction, while GSHHG owns the coast.
preparation.style: Union CWH/MH/CDF contextual display geometry; fill internal style holes smaller than 50 km²; simplify 500 m preserving topology; union with complete marine area buffered 3 km; simplify final coverage at 250 m. The coastal extension is styling only and is removed at the exact GSHHG land clip.
preparation.output: Transform to WGS84 and round to1e-7degrees; run shared-arc Mapshaper cleanup without further simplification on land/water and separately on the admin partition. This removes independent-rounding slivers and ensures identical boundary vertices survive reprojection. No artboard fit baked in.

localTopologyProtection.reason: Mapshaper final cleanup merged narrow-channel islands into neighbouring land. Exact source land/water topology is restored locally, rather than accepting lost water gaps.

finalSharedTopologySerialization.method: Mapshaper clean gap-fill-area=0; no further simplification; shared arcs serialized once for land/water and separately for admin partition.

actualCanvasCoverage.waterSemantics: Inland water only; acquisition domain includes legitimate ocean.

lakeCandidateSelection.explanation: The ArcGIS envelope query supplies a conservative candidate set. Exact local geometric clipping removes wholly outside candidates. The independent projected polygon query was checked by the acquisition agent against the same exact set.

limitations: Exactly clipped means identical derived land geometry is reused for fill and hatch; it does not mean a surveyed or current legal coastline.

Marine coastlines use GSHHG2.3.7 (2017), based on older WVS source data. Major BC lakes/manmade waters are supplemented from the official Freshwater Atlas; waterbodies below1km² and other omitted classes are outside this selection. Non-BC inland water retains older GSHHG/WDBII coverage.

Regional 125 m generalization can change small island shape and area. All 8,315 selected source land/water components were retained or locally restored; 75 narrow-channel islands required exact source topology within 250 m. Final coordinate rounding can cause subpixel area changes.

The coastal coverage is decorative, broadly informed by CWH/MH/CDF BEC zones, with internal style holes below50km² filled and a3km marine/coastal extension. It is not an ecological inventory or current forest-cover classification.

The data extend beyond the requested lon/lat bounds because the complete rectangular BC Albers drawing canvas includes margins and corners outside those bounds. Coverage is validated against the actual drawing extent, not only the requested projected view.
The regional US context is an administrative complement, not a complete national polygon.

correctedKamloopsCheckpoint.reason: Use verified interior point from official FWA polygon rather than the initial approximate location. GSHHG genuinely omitted the body, but the initial point was also outside the official lake.

canadianRoadsAndPlaces.dataset: Rainforest to Rockies geographic illustration – bounded highway and place subset
canadianRoadsAndPlaces.coordinateReferenceSystem: WGS84 / EPSG:4326; GeoJSON longitude, latitude order
processing: Query all five NRN route-number fields within the padded WGS84 extent; request source geometry in EPSG:4326 at six decimal places without server-side generalization.
Verify every query page hash, expected source count, and unique provincial OBJECTID before processing.
Exclude only source classes Ramp and Service Lane. Retain all other selected, numbered through-road classes; do not infer access or road condition.
Clip source LineStrings to the padded extent, project each segment into EPSG:3005, then simplify each at 75 m with topology preservation and unchanged segment endpoints.
Attribute concurrent routes from all five route-number fields. Remove only coordinate-identical duplicate lines within each province and route.

Merge exactly shared line endpoints within each province and route; preserve disconnected components and separate carriageways. Do not node incidental crossings, average carriageways, snap nearby points, add missing links, or infer ferries.
Return WGS84 coordinates rounded to six decimals. This final rounding is additional to the measured 75 m simplification bound and is less than 0.08 m within this extent.
Retain official generalized CGNDB place points and a US Census Seattle internal point. Do not snap city or mountain anchors to highways.

rendering.layerOrder: Draw supporting roads first, then primary roads so a concurrent supporting route does not add dashes over a primary stroke.
rendering.pathRule: Render source polylines directly. Avoid a free smoothing spline that can leave the actual road corridor.

limitations: This is an illustrated-scale road subset, not a routing network or a complete road inventory. Ramps, service lanes, unrequested route numbers, and US roads are not included.
NRN data are a current service snapshot at retrieval; individual source segment currency can vary. No claim of real-time road status, closure, legal access, or navigability is made.
Merged part counts do not imply separate journey routes: junctions, carriageways and branches can remain as separate genuine source components.
geometryLengthKm totals the retained geometry, including distinct carriageways and route concurrency; it is not a driving distance or an official route length.
There is no invented Victoria–Vancouver ferry or Seattle highway connector. Vancouver Island and mainland Highway 1 remain separate actual road geometry.
BC 93A and Alberta 95 were queried but are absent from this selected source extent; no geometry was substituted.
The Mount Robson peak and populated locality are distinct supplied anchors. The peak lies away from Highway 16 and must not be drawn as a roadside stop.
Victoria's city point is not the Mile 0 monument. Any Mile 0 emblem positioned nearby is a decorative design cue unless independently sourced.

washingtonI5.dataset: Official WSDOT I-5 mainline supplement, Canadian border through Seattle
washingtonI5.useConstraintsSummary: WSDOT disclaims liability and fitness for a particular purpose; see source metadata for the full terms. No CC or OGL licence is asserted.
washingtonI5.selection: RouteID = '005' selects only the mainline, preserving both increasing and decreasing carriageway directions. Related ramp/frontage/local-access route identifiers are excluded.
washingtonI5.processing: Bounded official service query without server generalization. Clip to the stated Seattle-border envelope; simplify each segment independently at75 m in EPSG:3005 with topology preservation and unchanged endpoints. Remove only exactly duplicate lines; merge exactly shared endpoints; return WGS84 rounded to six decimals. No free smoothing, endpoint snapping, connectors, or ferry geometry.
washingtonI5.endpointMeaning: Northern endpoints are the supplied road ends near the border. Southern ends are clipped at latitude47.55, just south of central Seattle; this is a map-study extent, not an official I-5 terminus. The Census Seattle point remains unchanged and is not connected by an invented spur.
washingtonI5.sourceAccuracyNote: WSDOT metadata says positional accuracy has not been determined. The measured simplification tolerance does not establish source positional accuracy.

roads.integration: Append WSDOT I-5 as a supporting geographic road; retain the 7.506 m source gap at the Canada/US border and separate carriageways. No synthetic connection. Preserve all generalized place points.

provenance.construction: Project source geometry once to EPSG:3005; use one uniform scale for every feature. Province regions and decorative coverage are intersected with one shared dry-land geometry. No coastal inset or white shore stroke.
provenance.motifPlacement: Decorative regional motifs, not recorded observations or inventories. Route badges are snapped to the corresponding real centreline.
